text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — running an eviction-readiness checkpoint tomorrow 09:30 PT. Focus: mixed-capacity pools, spot -> on-demand failover, and KV cache warmup behavior. I want a short canary then expand if healthy.

Priya: +1. I can own the us-west-2 pathing and routing checks. Do we have an agreed success criteria? :eyes: 

Matt: Can we keep this as a 10% canary traffic slice? No full cutovers. Also prefer evict-sim rather than hard deletes so we don't blow up images or PVs.

Alex: Exactly — canary 10% for 15m, then optional 30% if metrics look good. Success criteria I propose: p95 request failover time < 12s, overall 5m error rate delta < 0.5%, KV cache hit ratio drop < 10 percentage points, autoscaler spend bump < 20% above baseline for the window.

Jordan: Add cost gating: if on-demand consumption > 20% over baseline for 10m, we auto-abort and rollback. Also alert channel will be #eng-sre-incidents.

Priya: Here's the short playbook I'll follow. Posting commands we plan to use (simulate evictions with internal tool):

```bash
# simulate eviction of 2 GPUs in the mixed pool (us-west-2)
./infractl sim-evict --cluster prod-usw2 --pool gpu-mixed --count 2 --reason game-day

# roll traffic to canary route
./routerctl set-weight --route llm-api --subset canary --weight 10
```

Matt: Good. We'll also run a targeted promote-to-on-demand test after the first eviction to ensure fallback capacity is available. I'll have a small script to watch queue length and worker churn.

Alex: PromQLs for quick checks (add to the dashboard):

```promql
# eviction events
sum(rate(node_evictions_total{pool=\"gpu-mixed\"}[1m])) by (zone)

# KV cache hit ratio (per model)
sum(kv_cache_hits_total{model=~\".*\"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups_total{model=~\".*\"})

# request failover time p95
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(failover_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

Jordan: I'll wire an alert: "EvictionGameDay: Failover p95 > 12s" -> page primary oncall. Also add a non-pager inform to #eng-sre if KV drop > 15% so we can watch degradation.

Linh: I'll be oncall for this window. My plan: watch the canary, validate model output quality (sanity prompts), and confirm no silent throttling in the runtime. If anything looks off, flip canary weight to 0 and run rollback.

Priya: One more check — ensure autoscaler policy has prevention for sudden cold-starts. If reactive scaleup latency > 30s repeatedly, abort. Who can own the autoscaler guard? @Matt?

Matt: I got autoscaler guard. I'll set temporary limits: max-on-demand-burst = +30% and cooldown = 90s for the run. If we hit the burst, script will restore weights and notify.

Alex: Communication plan: brief pre-run in #eng-sre at 09:10 PT with status. Post-run summary in this thread. Owner list: Priya (routing), Matt (autoscaler), Jordan (alerts), Linh (oncall), Alex (run lead).

sre-bot: Scheduled game-day: eviction-readiness-checkpoint; start=2026-03-19T16:30:00Z; watchers=5

Priya: Link to docs & checklist: https://go/repro/eviction-readiness (contains runbook, dashboards, rollback steps). Please review before 09:00 PT.

Jordan: small note — test in eu-west-1 will be more constrained due to limited spare on-demand capacity. Keep the eu slice at 5% if we test there.

Alex: Noted. I'll update the runbook to set eu limit 5%. Any objections?

Matt: No objections. :thumbsup:

Linh: I'll be available 09:00-10:30 PT. Will add short checklist to the runbook for model QA probes.

Priya: OK team — see you tomorrow. I'll paste the final checklist at 09:05 PT. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Thanks all. Post-run we'll capture lessons and a short retro (10 min) to refine the eviction automations. :party_parrot:
